change: The filesystem domain now supplies Effect.scoped at its existing named Effect.fn owner. Every return, failure or interruption releases its acquired native kernel before returning to the caller.
HTTP, service binding and nested Python/JavaScript/TypeScript filesystem callers share that owner. No new cache, service, transport, policy fallback, migration or native Rust binary is introduced.
The benchmark and regression forward native R2 calls, observe the shared kernel module memory capacity, and derive metric reports from one Effect Schema contract.

measurementDefinitions.kernelMemory: WebAssembly.Memory buffer capacity high-water for the kernel instance, captured after the request. Memory cannot shrink; fresh Workers isolate each phase. This is not RSS, live allocations, total Worker memory or Python heap.
measurementDefinitions.headBodyBytes: Sum of declared sizes of returned full bodies for the sandbox head key; the valid workload consumes those bodies. This is not network-wire or billable transferred bytes.
measurementDefinitions.counts: GET/conditional GET/full-body and PUT observations on that sandbox head key, not a count of every R2 operation in the process lifecycle.
measurementDefinitions.elapsed: Native Worker clock around handleRequest and response-text consumption; excludes seeding, Worker startup and RPC transport.

result.interpretation: Repeatable reduction in kernel linear-memory capacity for this workload. Full-head reads remain unchanged. Local time differences are small and tail results are mixed; no general latency, CPU or billing improvement is established.

comparisons.scope: All raw warmups, phases and measured samples retained. First run precedes metric-contract centralization; second run uses the final shared Schema. Measured Worker bytes are unchanged by that type-only refinement.

prevention: The filesystem action owns acquisition and release. A native high-water regression checks repeated successful and caught-failure calls; an outer request scope alone cannot enforce this lifetime.
limits: Only the measured repeated-metadata workload has comparative memory/timing evidence; maximum-scale roots, other domain lifetimes, arbitrary workloads and production remain unverified.
Native allocator capacity cannot shrink in an already grown isolate. A deployment starts new code/isolates; this source has not been deployed.
Fresh reads, authority checks and conditional publication remain; no R2 request reduction or AgentOS cost advantage is claimed.
